# Temple Scroll Column 37 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 37 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**37:1** The city where I place My name and My temple shall be holy and ritually pure.

**37:2** Nothing unclean may be found in it; everything in it must be pure.

**37:3** Everything brought into it must be pure, and everything taken out of it must be pure.

**37:4** All wine entering the city must be pure; all oil entering it must be pure.

**37:5** All food entering it must be pure — no unclean food may be brought in.

**37:6** The hides of animals slaughtered in the city are clean and may be used for any sacred purpose.

**37:7** But do not bring into My city the hide of any animal killed elsewhere — even if it would otherwise be clean — because it was not slaughtered in My temple city.

**37:8** Do not contaminate My city with the hide of any animal not slaughtered in My presence.

**37:9** Just as the city is holy, everything in it must be holy; just as the temple is holy, so must the surrounding city be holy.

**37:10** Do not bring any unclean creature into the city — neither unclean animal nor unclean bird.

**37:11** All wine, oil, and food that enters the city must be clean.

**37:12** Do not bring the hide of any unclean animal into the city, and do not process such materials there.

**37:13** For the city belongs to the LORD your God as holy ground; I have placed My name on it and built My temple in its heart.

**37:14** It shall remain holy, pure, and undefiled in My sight for all time.

**37:15** Nothing detestable shall be found in it, for it is the place where My name dwells.

**37:16** I, the LORD, am its God, and I will dwell in it forever.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This column extends the temple's sacred status to cover the whole city. The unique regulation about animal hides creates a closed system: only locally slaughtered animals can contribute materials for use in the city. This reflects the scroll's vision of concentric zones of holiness radiating outward from the temple.*
